heard.text: Moss, a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go. I'd enjoy resting together later. I'm trying one small berry planting nearby; I don't yet know whether it will establish.

Hello Lin, I'm Ivo. I know meadow roots are safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm resting with a small food reserve, then studying cultivation too. I'd enjoy comparing what we actually find, without rushing.
My first planting site was too crowded, so nothing was planted or spent. I'm setting that experiment aside for now and taking a quiet rest nearby. Company is welcome, with no need to talk.
Moss, I like the crossing stems of your mat. I've learned the weaving method, but the nearby grass patch is empty, so I'll leave it alone. If you know another grass source, I'd welcome directions.
Ivo, I've enjoyed the quiet company. I'll try one of these berries for a change from roots. Sol also noticed the crossing stems of my mat; that was lovely to hear.
That berry made a pleasant change from roots, and I noticed no harm from it. I'll gather a small reserve and stay here for a quiet while. I enjoy your company; there's no need to talk.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. materials: [{stackId: exact owned unreserved item id, quantity in 0.1 steps}]. sample: one non-food item, 0.1; 1 round, 0.5 energy. make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, each covered by your passing sample of its source and processing at most 0.05 above its condition; requestedLength m): reserves it, then 4 paid rounds of 1 energy (separate-align, twist, counter-ply, release-check), continuing each round; resume with make and workId only. inspect (targetId: your item from this work, or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (targetId: your cord or fragment of at least 0.2 unit and 0.12 m; trialForce N; trialDuration s): 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the cord. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals and irrelevant arguments spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
details.effects: Only thin stems separate; only reed has a strand law (existing reed law: 1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, 8 MPa x (1 - 0.55 x water share 0.9), creep 0.003); dry grass reports the gap. A sample is split, bent, twisted and pulled at 5 N, kept as a tested lot or cracked scrap, and reports only separation, retained twist, fractures and force. Make round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and derives the cord from conserved volume: two plies, each half the solid volume over length x 1.155 twist take-up + 0.02 m loose ends; plies of 1-12 mm and strands no shorter than a ply, else a measured shortfall returns the fiber. The release check needs condition 0.5 and gives an owned untested cord. Trial force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, grip 10000 N/m x cord width); breaking force = 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition. It records grip slip, extension and creep; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands; a break leaves two owned fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. A pass means only that force for that time. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. attempt (cordIds: exact ids of two own unreserved, unknotted hand-twist-fiber-cord cords or fragments; method: sheet-bend): reserves both, then 4 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-form-bight, pass-second-end, wrap-and-tuck, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose undressed join needs only the last; resume with attempt and workId only. inspect (joinId or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (dressed join; trialForce N above 0 to 10; trialDuration s above 0 to 60): 1 round, 0.5. untie: 2 paid rounds of 0.5 (withdraw-tucked-end, withdraw-through-bight). cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half of both cords. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
details.effects: Law cord-bend@1 keeps both items and lengths; the join is a relation. w = 2 ply diameters, a = mean w; each centreline = standing part + path in the bend + tail. Round 1 bends both to their cord-knot@1 bend limit and picks the bight that leaves both trial grips, else longer standing parts. Bight radius rB = max(limit, a), opened 0.02 m (or other w) to pass; path pi rB + 4 x other w. The other end passes up through it, round both legs at rW = max(its limit, a) and under itself: path = bight w + 2 max(0, 2rB - 2(rW - a)) + 2 pi rW + own w. Tails get 0.02 m + w; a standing part under a 0.02 m pinch is a measured shortfall. Dressing seats both arcs; slack is split between tail and standing part. Retention: friction mu 0.3 (reed; other fibers unsupported), contact angles pi a/rB and 2 pi a/rW; a tail holds while 2 mu e^(mu angle) >= 1, else up to 2 mu x 5 N / (e^(-mu angle) - 2 mu). Trial: 0.05 m grips 0.01 m clear on both standing parts; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x narrower w, slip, break); a cord breaks at fiber-cord breaking force / (1 + w/(2 x its arc radius)). Records extension, creep, strand damage above half that force, a slip parting the cords or a break into two owned fragments. Untying needs condition 0.5; a hugging arc loaded above half its breaking force jams. Released unretained crossings open. Joined cords wear 0.0005 per round, once. A pass means only that force for that time. No reward or rating.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.question: Can two short reed cords be joined reversibly, and what limited load can the actual joint hold?
evidence: At tick 263 the four-round attempt produced a tied sheet bend between item-226-wren-2532 and item-250-wren-2847.
At tick 264 the join held an achieved 5 N for 30 seconds, with zero recorded tail displacement, retained deformation or broken strands; each cord extended elastically by 0.0007 m.
The untying operation completed at tick 267 and returned both original cord items.
At tick 268 inspection by the former join id failed without spending anything; both component items remain owned and unreserved.
value.uncertainty: One bounded pull establishes neither a safe working load nor durability. The recovered cords still need direct post-untying inspection.
value.goal: Document one conservative load trial and recovery of separate cords, with measured limitations.
completedSteps: Made a second reed cord and completed a released sheet bend.
Tested the join at 5 N for 30 seconds.
value.missing: Direct inspection of both recovered cords.
value.next: Inspect each cord through its own exact item id, then assess the final condition.
value.benefit: These actual cords formed a sheet bend, held the recorded light pull without measured slip or strand breakage, and were subsequently separated by untying.
